main_text.p: Sitwolbatdun, Septuplum: quasi sevenwoudt] Hoc nobis sevenfold, à Sax. reofonpealo ȝ
Sten-ogun, Pupilla oculi] Hoc Sax. reon-eazan, quasi Visus oculi, à reon, Sax. videre, & eaz; oculus, alias æpl; unde nostratium Apple of the Eye.
Sigtmart, Victor. in Tacito, Segl-merus] Victoria, Sax. rige: victorio-fus, rigæpest: Mart autem hic in Sig-tmart, à mæpe duclum arbitror, quod magnum, celebrem, præstantem sonat.

Slaptgravt, Sepulcrum: suprà Burgift] Sepulcrum nobis hodie a grave, à Sax. grave; Verstegano slapigrava, q. sleep-grave, quia (inquit) sepultus tanquam dormiens habendus est. Conjecturam probo, cum dormire, nobis sit to sleep, à Sax. slapan. Sepulcrum hinc vocatur Dormitorium.
Slabta, Generatio: & slabsen, femini. Nos compositè Geslacht.
Sptetis, Hasta. Nos spleste. Nomen primogenium à mucrone, sptets] Hoc Belg. spet, speet, unde forte nostrum spit, Veru. Hasta autem Sax. rpepe, quod nobis manset.

page.notes: Old-German and Anglo-Saxon words are in black letter and Greek-like forms; several readings (e.g. "reofonpealo", "rigæpest", "rpepe", "manset") are uncertain. The handwritten "243" and the printed running head are as seen; the text is a glossary and some entries may be misread.
